baseline_models.focus_anchor: عِبْرَةً (ع ب ر) joined to لِمَن يَخْشَىٰ (خ ش ي).
baseline_models.mechanism: The focus noun names admonition by making one witnessed condition cross over into another condition against which the hearer measures the self; awe-laden fear makes that transfer consequential rather than merely clever.

activation_trace.role: Making one condition an admonitory analogue for another supplies the lesson's basic operation.
Passage from side to side gives the analogy a spatial image: the reader crosses from the cited case to the self.
Fear joined with awe supplies the receptive pressure that turns analogy into warning.

changed_reading.before: There is a lesson in that for a fearful person.
changed_reading.after: There is a crossing from the observed case to one's own possible condition, and awe is what lets that crossing become admonition.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: عِبْرَةً can activate the transfer from an appearance to its meaning, while يَخْشَىٰ can carry a knowledge-adjacent branch.
baseline_models.mechanism: The focus can describe an interpretive act: the reader does not stop at the surface of ذَٰلِكَ but moves from what appears to the hidden import it bears. The knowledge branch of خشية makes this an apprehending awe, without erasing ordinary fear.

activation_trace.role: Interpreting a vision by moving from its outward appearance to its meaning supplies the model of semantic transfer.
The figurative knowledge branch lets fear include recognition of what the presented case means.

changed_reading.before: The event contains a ready-made moral statement.
changed_reading.after: The event must be interpreted across the gap between visible occurrence and inwardly grasped import by a knower whose understanding has the quality of awe.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: عِبْرَةً and the recipient construction لِمَن يَخْشَىٰ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The lesson behaves like meaning carried through expression into a recipient. The prepositional recipient is not incidental: the event becomes an effective message only upon reaching a hearer disposed to awe.

activation_trace.role: Meaning passing through speech to a hearer supplies a communicative rather than merely observational lesson.
Awe-filled fear identifies the disposition in which the transmitted meaning takes effect.

changed_reading.before: The lesson is an object lying in the event.
changed_reading.after: The event carries an argument toward a recipient, and awe completes that communicative passage.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding endpoint turns the baseline analogy into explicit deterrence: Pharaoh is seized for guilt, and his punishment is characterized by a branch whose function is to restrain someone other than the punished person. Thus his case is built to cross into the later observer's conduct.

activation_trace.role: Analogical admonition supplies the focus operation that the preceding punishment activates.
Being taken to account for wrongdoing makes the seizure a consequence and supplies the punished case.
Punishment that deters someone other than its recipient makes the case explicitly transferable to an observer.

structural_cues: 79:15-25 is a narrated sequence whose punitive endpoint stands immediately before ذَٰلِكَ in 79:26.
The indefinite عِبْرَةً is followed by the beneficiary phrase لِمَن يَخْشَىٰ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies accountable seizure, other-directed deterrent punishment, and analogical admonition; I infer the arrow from Pharaoh's consequence to the hearer's self-restraint. A live alternative is that نَكَالَ only intensifies Pharaoh's own punishment rather than specifying the lesson's transmission.

changed_reading.before: Pharaoh's end is one morally instructive event.
changed_reading.after: Pharaoh's end is deliberately made into an other-facing deterrent: the punished case is meant to be carried across into the fearful observer's choices.

context_deltas.mechanism: The lesson can be read as a diagnostic sequence rather than a single maxim: exceeding the limit becomes denial and disobedience, then collective mobilization, then a claim of supreme elevation. عبرة asks the hearer to recognize this repeatable escalation before its terminal seizure.

activation_trace.role: Comparison with another condition lets the hearer map the narrated stages onto a still-developing present case.
Exceeding a limit in disobedience supplies the initiating boundary violation.
Contradiction of truth supplies the refusal that follows the shown sign.
Departure from obedience turns denial into enacted resistance.
Driving and gathering a group toward a purpose expands private refusal into organized power.
Greatness as domineering self-exaltation supplies the trajectory's culminating claim.

structural_cues: The verbs in 79:17-24 advance from transgression through refusal and public action to the supremacy claim.
79:25 follows that sequence with seizure before 79:26 names the عبرة.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an ordered series of acts and branch images; I infer a causal escalation and a diagnostic use for it. The materially live alternative is a rhetorical list of Pharaoh's acts without a claim that every later tyrannical course follows the same order.

changed_reading.before: The lesson is simply that arrogance is punished.
changed_reading.after: The lesson is a recognizable escalation map, allowing the fearful reader to identify and interrupt transgression before it matures into mobilized supremacy.

context_deltas.mechanism: The interpretive-transfer baseline acquires an ethical direction. Moses offers purification and gentle guidance toward fear, then shows a manifest sign; عبرة is the successful movement from what is displayed outwardly to inward reform, a movement Pharaoh blocks by denial.

activation_trace.role: Transfer from an appearance to its meaning supplies the focus's interpretive movement.
Purity and rectification supply the inward destination proposed before the sign is shown.
Gentle indication toward the true way supplies the path from address to changed orientation.
Showing and making visible supplies the outward presentation that still requires uptake.
A manifest sign supplies legible evidence rather than a hidden premise.

structural_cues: 79:18-20 orders an invitation to purification, guidance toward the Lord and fear, and the showing of the great sign.
79:21 marks the failed uptake immediately after the sign.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies visible evidence and a proposed path of purification and guidance; I infer that عبرة names the conversion of the former into the latter. The alternative is that the sign only authenticates Moses and that purification is a separate invitation rather than the lesson's destination.

changed_reading.before: Taking the lesson means correctly decoding what the event signifies.
changed_reading.after: Taking the lesson means carrying a manifest sign across into purification, guided orientation, and awe; correct recognition is incomplete until it reforms the observer.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening dispute gives the passage branch of عبرة a temporal and ontological scale. The deniers ask about being returned after becoming decayed bones, but one driving cry moves them abruptly into a new scene; the lesson can train the reader to cross imaginatively from the present state to the otherwise denied return.

activation_trace.role: Passage from one side to another supplies the focus anchor for transition between states.
Return to a prior place or condition supplies the transition the speakers dispute.
Decay supplies the apparently impassable starting state.
Coming back again supplies the recurrence mocked as loss.
A forceful vocal drive supplies the abrupt means by which the disputed transition occurs.

structural_cues: 79:10-12 voices incredulity about return after decay.
79:13-14 answers the question with a single cry and immediate arrival on the exposed ground.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a denied return, bodily decay, recurrence, and abrupt arrival; I infer that these activate عبرة as mentally crossing between states. A live alternative keeps ذَٰلِكَ narrowly tied to the Moses account and treats the resurrection sequence only as thematic framing.

changed_reading.before: The lesson compares one historical moral case with another.
changed_reading.after: The lesson also exercises the capacity to pass from the visible present to a denied future state, making resurrection thinkable as a transition rather than an isolated assertion.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately after the focus, the discourse changes evidence domains from punished ruler to constructed cosmos. The crossing and analogy branches of عبرة make 79:26 a hinge: the reader trained to transfer consequence from Pharaoh's case is next asked to transfer observed ordered creation into confidence about re-creation and judgment.

activation_trace.role: Using one condition as an analogue for another supplies the reasoning operation shared across evidence domains.
Crossing from side to side supplies the hinge image for the discourse's move from history to cosmos.
Bringing creation into existence supplies the new domain of evidence.
Building by joining parts supplies an image of deliberate cosmic construction.
Integrity and completed proportion supply ordered completion rather than raw magnitude.
Fixing and stabilizing supplies the grounded endpoint of the construction sequence.

structural_cues: 79:27 opens directly after the focus with a comparative question about the difficulty of human and heavenly creation.
79:27-33 proceeds through building, proportioning, provisioning, and anchoring before returning to judgment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the immediate genre shift and a sequence of ordered creation; I infer that the focus's transfer mechanism helps bridge historical consequence to cosmic proof. The alternative is that 79:27 begins an independent argument and 79:26 only closes the Pharaoh account.

changed_reading.before: The lesson closes the historical story behind it.
changed_reading.after: The lesson also functions as a hinge that teaches transfer across evidence domains, from historical reversal to the ordered creation invoked for resurrection and judgment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing contrast operationalizes the focus's يَخْشَىٰ. Fear is anticipation at the station of one's Lord that restrains the self from its inclination; it is not only an emotion that permits recognition but a stance that interrupts action. This supplies the behavioral endpoint of عبرة.

activation_trace.role: Fear with awe supplies the focus disposition that the closing contrast makes behavioral.
Admonition by comparison supplies the lesson whose successful uptake needs an observable effect.
Fear that anticipates harm supplies the prospective force of accountability.
A station or standing-place gives the anticipated encounter a stable orientation before the Lord.
Restraint and prevention supply the behavioral action produced by fear.
The self as one's own identity supplies the internal object to be governed.
The soul's inclination supplies the competing direction that restraint blocks.

structural_cues: 79:37-41 contrasts two parallel مَنْ cases and their destinations.
79:40 binds fear of the Lord's station directly to restraining the self from inclination.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies anticipatory fear, a station before the Lord, self-restraint, and inclination; I infer that this later contrast specifies how the focus recipient uses the lesson. The alternative is that 79:40 states an independent criterion for salvation without defining the earlier يَخْشَىٰ.

changed_reading.before: The one who fears is emotionally receptive to a lesson.
changed_reading.after: The one who fears anticipates standing before the Lord and converts the lesson into governance of the self against its contrary inclination.

context_deltas.mechanism: The final warning formula repeats the focus's fear-qualified audience and clarifies the communicative model: warning is directed effectively to the one who fears it. Thus لِمَن in 79:26 marks not ownership of information but the recipient in whom the narrated message becomes active.

activation_trace.role: Meaning carried through expression to a listener supplies the baseline communicative passage.
Awe-filled fear supplies the recipient disposition named in the focus.
Warning that frightens and awakens caution states the communicative action that the lesson performs.

structural_cues: 79:26 says لِمَن يَخْشَىٰ and 79:45 closes with مُنذِرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰهَا.
Both constructions select the fear-responsive person rather than asserting equal uptake by every hearer.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated fear-qualified recipient and the awakening function of warning; I infer that the final formula clarifies how عبرة reaches its audience. The alternative is that the repetition only identifies the same pious group without describing a transmission mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The lesson exists equally for all, though fearful people appreciate it more.
changed_reading.after: The lesson is a warning-event whose communicative circuit closes in the fear-responsive hearer, where fright awakens caution.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because عِبْرَةً in the focus most directly supports admonition, yet the supplied ع ب ر inventory also contains flowing tears and hot grief, while the surah supplies trembling hearts, seeing eyes lowered in submission, and awe. It remains anchored as an affective resonance linking the focus noun and يَخْشَىٰ; downstream prose should present it as wordplay or embodied undertone, not replace 'lesson' with 'tear.'
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The tear-and-grief branch of ع ب ر at عِبْرَةً, held together with the awe branch of يَخْشَىٰ.

activation_trace.role: Flowing tears and hot grief supply a bodily undertone to the focus noun.
Fear with awe connects the tear resonance to the explicitly named recipient disposition.
The heart as the affective organ supplies the locus of the response.
Agitation and heart-throbbing give the response a somatic pulse.
Physical sight supplies the eye through which the response is registered.
Lowering and submission turn the eye's response into embodied humility.

changed_reading.before: The lesson is cognitively inferred by someone afraid.
changed_reading.after: As an exploratory undertone, the lesson passes through an affected heart and lowered eye, becoming the kind of awe that can tremble, grieve, and even draw tears.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because the focus noun conventionally names admonition and 79:46 comes later, but the supplied passage image for ع ب ر and the closing collapse of worldly duration into one evening or morning make a temporal-transit resonance possible. It remains anchored in the focus root; downstream prose should call it a secondary existential echo, not claim that عِبْرَةً lexically means death or that ذَٰلِكَ points forward to 79:46.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The side-to-side passage branch of ع ب ر at عِبْرَةً.

activation_trace.role: Passing from one side to another supplies the image of life as transit rather than settled duration.
Remaining in a place supplies the duration that retrospective vision radically contracts.
The evening interval supplies one brief boundary used to measure the apparently long stay.

changed_reading.before: The observer crosses from another person's case to a moral conclusion.
changed_reading.after: As a secondary echo, the observer also recognizes personal life as a brief crossing whose apparent length collapses when the final state is seen.

strongest_changes: The immediate نَكَال endpoint makes the Pharaoh account an explicitly other-directed deterrent rather than a generic historical moral.
The closing contrast turns خشية from receptive emotion into anticipatory self-restraint before the Lord.
The resurrection and creation sequences activate عبرة as a crossing operation between states and evidence domains.
summary.what_was_special: The focus's compact pairing of عبرة and خشية works simultaneously as analogy, interpretive transfer, and message reception. Whole-surah context makes those operations behavioral: a displayed sign should cross into reform, a punished trajectory should cross into deterrence, and fear should cross into restraint.
remaining_uncertainties: ذَٰلِكَ most naturally closes the Pharaoh sequence, while the opening and following creation passages may activate the function of عبرة without enlarging its grammatical referent.
The knowledge branch of خشية can sharpen awe as recognition, but should not displace the direct fear-and-awe branch.
The tear and life-passage readings remain resonances requiring explicit qualification rather than primary lexical renderings.
